builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Process-Knowledge-Guided Latent Diffusion for Generative Design of Porous Architectures: A Case Study in Aerosol Jet Printing
summary: The technique replaces unguided or domain-only conditioned latent diffusion sampling for porous layout design by adding a ControlNet domain branch and a separately trained score regressor whose gradients steer each denoising step toward process-suitable layouts. It costs training and maintaining a VQ-VAE, a topology U-Net, a ControlNet branch, and a surrogate regressor, plus a process model for the score, and guidance at high weights requires tuning (score improved only past weight 300, with 12,000 needed for the reported gain). It can fail if the surrogate regressor mispredicts scores on noised latents, if the flow-focusing process model misrepresents actual deposition, or if results from seven modeled flow settings and four evaluation domains do not transfer to other processes or geometries.
rationale: The method addresses process-specific porous layout generation for aerosol jet printing, a manufacturing design problem outside the reader's LLM/ML production scope, and its gains are validated on only four domains under stated assumptions.
technique: Process-knowledge-guided latent diffusion for porous design

claims.statement: The technique replaces unguided or domain-only conditioned latent diffusion sampling for porous layout design by adding a ControlNet domain branch and a separately trained score regressor whose gradients steer each denoising step toward process-suitable layouts. It costs training and maintaining a VQ-VAE, a topology U-Net, a ControlNet branch, and a surrogate regressor, plus a process model for the score, and guidance at high weights requires tuning (score improved only past weight 300, with 12,000 needed for the reported gain). It can fail if the surrogate regressor mispredicts scores on noised latents, if the flow-focusing process model misrepresents actual deposition, or if results from seven modeled flow settings and four evaluation domains do not transfer to other processes or geometries.

Regressor-gradient guidance reduced the mean process-dependent utilization score from 0.642 (domain conditioning alone) to 0.450 at guidance weight 12,000 (112 samples per weight; lower is better), a roughly 1.43x improvement on three validation domains and one test domain.
